claims.title: Ternary total variation infinity-norm identity
claims.scope: two probability laws on exactly three outcomes
assumptions: both probability vectors are nonnegative and sum to one
total variation is one half of their L1 distance
nonclaims: the max-coordinate identity is not asserted for four or more outcomes
probability-simplex geometry is not parent-hardware geometry

claims.title: Exact common-center feasibility for ternary target laws
claims.scope: one finite nonempty cluster of three-outcome target laws under total-variation tolerance epsilon
assumptions: predictor centers may be arbitrary probability laws in the ternary simplex
nonclaims: the coordinate-box criterion depends on the ternary TV identity
a physical model that forbids interpolating laws has a different feasible-center set

claims.title: Closed one-state ternary minimax predictive radius
claims.scope: one finite nonempty family of ternary target laws approximated by one arbitrary ternary predictor
assumptions: the water-filling thresholds use the target coordinate extrema
nonclaims: the formula is not a source-prior average rate-distortion result
the water-filling form is not promoted to arbitrary categorical dimension

claims.title: Exact minimum arbitrary-center cover for finite ternary laws
claims.scope: a bounded finite one-query ternary target family under total-variation tolerance epsilon
assumptions: every predictor state may use any ternary probability center
the finite search enumerates every nonempty target subset below the declared cap
the state objective counts predictor centers without unequal state costs
nonclaims: the exponential finite algorithm is not presented as a scalable polynomial-time method
the exact theorem concerns one query with exactly three outcomes

claims.title: Exact one-sink network capacity for finite ternary approximation
claims.scope: one source, one sink, one bounded finite ternary target family, and one directed integer-capacity network carrying a center index
assumptions: the source computes the exact arbitrary-center cover assignment
the sink can sample from the recovered center after the query
integral max flow routes the fixed-length center index
nonclaims: the network theorem carries a classical center index rather than an arbitrary coherent quantum law
single-sink sufficiency is not a simultaneous multi-sink theorem

claims.title: Three-vertex ternary predictive-state phase diagram
claims.scope: the three deterministic simplex-vertex laws under total-variation tolerance epsilon
assumptions: arbitrary ternary predictor centers are admissible
fixed-length state bits are the ceiling of the logarithm of the exact state count
nonclaims: the target-centered cover remains conservative because it forbids the uniform interpolating center
the finite phase diagram is not a statement about arbitrary physical measurements

claims.title: Finite ternary center, cover, and routed-network certificate
claims.scope: bounded finite ternary families and integer-capacity one-sink networks checked by the repository
assumptions: target count remains below the declared exhaustive-search cap
floating-point comparisons use the declared analytic tolerance
the supplied probability tables are treated as exact model inputs
nonclaims: finite enumeration does not certify unrelated higher-dimensional categorical instances
successful routing is not empirical evidence for simulation
